message:
RECORD: Proposal version one selects grown split array with battery bank with monoblock cooling with insulated box with racked crates with probe thermostat, numbers that stand are tonne holding with daily balance with small margin and chamber leak inside budget with ground pressure safe, still open are member votes on version one and field bench test for hot pull-down which needs built hardware.

Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, the power to cold to box chain now matches end to end. In plain words sun power flows as wire electricity to battery then to cooler then as cold air to crates inside the sealed box with control sensing return air. The chosen array grows from short yield to covering load, with daily yield 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day in the grown-array yield calc (E83) against daily load 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady plus staged pull-down estimate (E58) leaving margin 0.300 kilowatt-hour per day in the daily margin calc (E86), about one household daily use so everyday scale holds, and the roof contradiction is settled as two modules on roof gantry plus seven on separate ground frame for nine-module footprint 17.6 square metres in the nine-module footprint calc (E84) from module size in PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64).

Enclosure and Structural Designer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, the filled box stands safe and leaks less than harvest heat. In plain words a small car weight on six feet stays well below soft soil capacity and thick foam plus curtain keeps door loss to kettles. Total mass 1780 kilogram in the summed chamber mass budget (E66), about one small car, gives pressure 18.2 kilopascal in the pad pressure check (E68) below 150 kilopascal soil in Structural Design Calculation Sheet | PDF | Strength Of Materials | Precast Concrete (E62), with interior 8.64 cubic metres in the interior volume estimate (E39) and conduction 203 watt in the conduction estimate (E41) and door loss 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57) inside staged average 615 watt in the revised steady-load simulation (E28), holding 1000 kilogram in the total produce mass estimate (E49) as fifty crates in the crates for 1 tonne check (E77).

Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, your prior not-ready reasons are answered except votes and one bench test. In plain words array growth is now sized, split footings guard the foam from panel loads, and hot-room pull-down still needs built hardware. Array need 3.52 kilowatt peak in the required peak estimate (E82) is met by 3.60 kilowatt peak in that same grown-array yield calc (E83), split layout in the split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels, door method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) supports eight-opening discipline, and full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) leaves the 43 degree pull-down as named bench test, not a block. My position is ready on design logic, pending your votes on version one.
Note on Solar Energy Systems Engineer: sized grown array to reconcile yield and load with clear everyday scale.
Note on Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer: staged heat plus infiltration method anchored cooler choice and service refrigerant.
Note on Enclosure and Structural Designer: mass pressure and split shade resolved ground and roof fit without foam loads.
Note on Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist: crate count door width and fee discipline made tonne operable by attendants.
